idiom_name: class per table with static find and instance insert/update over node-postgres parameterised queries
implementation_notes: Node has no per-row persistence objects: the realization is a class whose instances mirror a row, a static find that runs a parameterised query and wraps the returned plain object back into the class, and instance insert/update/delete methods that call pool.query or a checked-out client. node-postgres returns rows as plain objects and only handles parameter substitution; knex adds query building, but in both cases the gateway class itself - identity, methods, mapping - is hand-written. ORMs such as Sequelize provide a different pattern (Active Record models), which is why a gateway here is a deliberate, small, explicit choice.
pitfalls: A transaction needs one checked-out client (pool.connect + BEGIN/COMMIT); calling pool.query per statement scatters the work over different connections.
pg returns bigint and numeric as strings unless type parsers are configured, so typed fields can be wrong at runtime.
Rows come back as plain objects: without explicitly re-wrapping them the result is not an instance of the gateway class and has no update method.
Forgetting await on a query produces an unhandled rejection and a write that appears to succeed.
